title: Fixed scripture width settings field sizing
summary: In Settings, the **Scripture Width** number used to be cut off once it reached 100 or more (only two digits fit). The box now grows to fit the number, so values like `100` or `192` show in full. The same change also makes the round knob on the **Keep screen awake** switch stay white when the switch is on; in dark mode it used to turn near-black.

links.label: Issue 2120: Scripture width gets cutoff when value is 100 or more.

setup.title: Use a computer, not a phone
setup.body: The **Scripture Width** control only appears on desktop-sized screens. Use a laptop or desktop with the browser window reasonably wide. Chrome or Edge is best for the main tests; one test also uses Firefox or Safari.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link at the top of this page. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the old version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac). Signing in is not needed.

setup.title: Open Settings
setup.body: Click the gear icon (**Settings**) at the bottom of the left sidebar. Scroll until you see **Scripture Width**, with a **−** button, a number followed by `ch`, and a **+** button.

tests.title: Three-digit widths show in full
tests.why: This is the bug from issue 2120: values of 100 or more were cut off.
steps: In **Scripture Width**, click the number, select it all, and type `100`.
Look at the number between the **−** and **+** buttons.
Change it to `150`, then to `192` (the largest allowed value).
expected: Each time, all three digits are visible, followed by `ch`. No digit is cut off or hidden.
The Bible text on the page gets wider as the number goes up.

tests.title: The box shrinks back for two-digit widths
steps: With the width at a three-digit value, select the number and type `60`.
expected: The number shows as `60` (then `59`, `58`, …) with no large empty gap before `ch`.
The **−**, number and **+** stay neatly on one line.

tests.title: Crossing 99 → 100 with the + button
steps: Click **+** three times, watching the number.
expected: It reads `99`, then `100`, then `101`, always fully visible. The **+** button moves over slightly to make room, and nothing overlaps.

tests.title: The width still looks right in Firefox or Safari
tests.why: The fix relies on a newer browser feature that lets a box grow to fit its text. Some browsers (notably Firefox) don't support it yet, so the box may look different there. Check that it is still usable.
steps: Open the preview link in Firefox (or Safari on a Mac).
expected: All three digits are visible and the **−**, number, `ch` and **+** are still on one line inside the settings panel. Note in your results if the number box looks much wider than needed or pushes anything out of the panel.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Width setting is remembered
steps: Reload the page and open **Settings** again.
expected: **Scripture Width** still shows `120`, in full, and the Bible text is still at that width.

tests.title: Keep screen awake switch, light and dark mode
tests.why: The PR also changed the switch's knob color, which isn't mentioned in the PR description. Before, in dark mode the knob turned near-black when the switch was on; now it stays white. Flag it if this looks wrong or hard to see.
steps: Click the **More** button (three dots) at the top of the left sidebar and look at **Keep screen awake**. Click it to turn it on, then off.
Switch the theme to **Dark** and repeat.
expected: In both themes, the switch slides right and fills with the app's main color when on, and slides back when off.
The round knob is white in both positions and clearly visible against the switch in both themes.

notCovered: Phone-width screens: the Scripture Width control is hidden there, so nothing to check.
